investigation.title: Remote Agent Creation Eval Failing: POST /api/agents Returns 409 Agent Quota Exceeded (limit is 100)
investigation.summary: The AURA observability eval for remote-agent-create (and all sibling remote-agent checks) is failing because POST /api/agents returns HTTP 409 with error code "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". The eval probe account's organization has reached the swarm agent hard limit of 100, preventing the eval runner from creating a new remote agent and leaving all required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) unpopulated.
investigation.rootCause: The production-api swarm backend is enforcing a per-organization agent quota of 100. The eval runner account's organization has hit or exceeded this limit, causing every attempt by the eval probe to call POST /api/agents to be rejected with a 409 conflict before any agent is created. Because agent creation is the shared upstream step for all three remote-agent checks, all three checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) fail with the identical error message. This is an eval infrastructure failure against the production API; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence to indicate a broader production outage.

sibling.remote-agent-state and sibling.remote-agent-runtime: both siblings carry the identical 409 message (sameMessage: true), indicating the failure originates at the shared agent-creation step, not in state-polling or runtime-chat logic downstream.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:102-110: contract requires vmIdPresent === true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready'] — neither assertion can be evaluated because the agent was never created.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — Eval probe org has accumulated 100 swarm agents (live or leaked) and hit the hard quota enforced by the swarm backend. Each eval run creates an agent; if cleanup (withCleanup) failed on prior runs, orphaned agents accumulate against the quota.
SECONDARY — A prior eval run's cleanup step failed silently, leaving one or more agents un-deleted and incrementally consuming quota until the limit was reached.
TERTIARY — The quota limit of 100 was recently lowered by a backend configuration change, causing an org that was previously under the limit to now be over it.

LOW CONFIDENCE — Commit 6b9c8b0 ('feat(observability): separate feature health from runtime evidence') touched all three implicated eval files (features.json, check-expectations.json, run-status-probes.mjs) roughly 7 hours before the failure; however, the suspect-change record shows no candidateTouchedPaths matching the eval runner logic and no matchedNeedles, so a causal link to the quota error is not supported by the supplied evidence.

investigation.rootCause: The swarm backend returned HTTP 409 with error code "conflict" and message "agent quota exceeded: limit is 100" on every POST /api/agents call made by the eval runner. The remote-agent-state probe depends on successfully creating a remote agent before it can poll state; because creation failed at the API boundary, the probe exited before writing any evidence, causing a complete contract gap for all four required fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state). This is an eval-infrastructure failure against the production-api environment: no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so a broader production outage cannot be asserted from this data alone.

investigation.title: Image Generation Stream Eval Failure: SESSION_OPEN_FAILED (404) on /api/generate/image/stream in production-api Runtime
investigation.summary: The AURA observability eval for check `image-generation-stream` (feature `media-generation`, runtime `production-api`) failed because the agent runtime returned a 404 on the `/api/generate/image/stream` endpoint, emitting a `SESSION_OPEN_FAILED` error frame instead of the expected `generation_completed` frame and image URL artifact. This is an eval-infrastructure failure localized to the `production-api` harness endpoint reachability; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigation.rootCause: The eval probe in `infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs` (lines 904–921) issued an SSE request to `/api/generate/image/stream` against the `production-api` runtime environment. The server responded with HTTP 404, which the stream translated into a `generation_error` frame with code `SESSION_OPEN_FAILED` and the message "agent runtime endpoint not found (404): the harness is unreachable or running an incompatible version." Because the session could not be opened, no `generation_completed` frame was emitted and no image URL was produced, causing both required evidence keys (`frameTypes`, `imageUrlPresent`) to be absent and the contract assertions to fail. The most likely immediate cause is that the agent runtime harness backing `/api/generate/image/stream` in the `production-api` environment is either not deployed, deployed at a different base URL than the eval runner is configured to use (`LOCAL_HARNESS_URL` / `SWARM_BASE_URL`), or is running an incompatible API version that no longer exposes this route. Commit 6b9c8b0 touched workflow and harness setup files (including `.github/actions/setup-harness-sibling/action.yml` and `.github/workflows/aura-observability.yml`) and is a low-confidence hypothesis that a misconfiguration was introduced there, but this is not proven by the available eval or source evidence.
proof: failed-check.evidence: stream emitted event=generation_error with code=SESSION_OPEN_FAILED and message 'agent runtime endpoint not found (404)' — the harness returned HTTP 404 before any generation frames could be produced.
failed-check.message: check message explicitly states '404' and instructs to verify LOCAL_HARNESS_URL / SWARM_BASE_URL configuration.

failed-check.timing: latencyMs=2351, far below the warningLatencyMs=180000 threshold, confirming the failure was an immediate connection/routing rejection, not a timeout.

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:159-167: the production-api variant of image-generation-stream is registered as required=false with statusImpact=informational, scoping the blast radius to informational status only.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — Harness not deployed or unreachable: The agent runtime harness serving /api/generate/image/stream is not running or not reachable at the URL the eval runner resolved from LOCAL_HARNESS_URL or SWARM_BASE_URL in the production-api environment at the time of the run (2026-06-15T15:41:05Z).

SECONDARY — Incorrect or missing harness URL configuration: LOCAL_HARNESS_URL or SWARM_BASE_URL is misconfigured, pointing to a host or path that does not expose /api/generate/image/stream, causing the 404 at the routing layer rather than the harness itself being absent.

TERTIARY — Incompatible harness version: The harness is deployed but at an API version that has removed or renamed the /api/generate/image/stream route, producing a genuine 404 from the harness rather than a network-level miss.

LOW-CONFIDENCE HYPOTHESIS — Workflow/harness setup change in commit 6b9c8b0: This commit touched .github/actions/setup-harness-sibling/action.yml and .github/workflows/aura-observability.yml among other CI files. If it altered how the harness sibling is started or how its URL is injected into the eval runner environment, it could have broken harness reachability. This is unproven — the commit's candidateTouchedPaths list is empty and the overlap is metadata-only (suspect-change.6b9c8b0, confidence=low).

At eval time (2026-06-15T15:41:11Z), the snapshot age was measured at 341 minutes, meaning the last successful publish occurred approximately 5 hours and 41 minutes prior — roughly around 2026-06-15T09:59Z. The snapshot itself is structurally valid (all other assertions pass: schemaVersion=1, source=github-actions, hasLiveSource=true, hasNonUnknownFeatureData=true, featureCount=16), so the failure is isolated to the freshness/staleness dimension, not snapshot content or site reachability.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Creation Eval Failing: POST /api/agents Returns 409 Agent Quota Exceeded (limit is 100)
investigations.summary: The AURA observability eval for remote-agent-create (and all sibling remote-agent checks) is failing because POST /api/agents returns HTTP 409 with error code "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". The eval probe account's organization has reached the swarm agent hard limit of 100, preventing the eval runner from creating a new remote agent and leaving all required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) unpopulated.
investigations.rootCause: The production-api swarm backend is enforcing a per-organization agent quota of 100. The eval runner account's organization has hit or exceeded this limit, causing every attempt by the eval probe to call POST /api/agents to be rejected with a 409 conflict before any agent is created. Because agent creation is the shared upstream step for all three remote-agent checks, all three checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) fail with the identical error message. This is an eval infrastructure failure against the production API; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence to indicate a broader production outage.
proof: failed-check.message: POST /api/agents failed with 409 — error body contains 'conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100', confirming the API rejected the creation request before any agent was provisioned.

failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}), confirming zero required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) were captured — consistent with the request failing before agent creation completed.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are listed as missing, matching the empty evidence object.

sibling.remote-agent-state and sibling.remote-agent-runtime: both siblings carry the identical 409 message (sameMessage: true), indicating the failure originates at the shared agent-creation step, not in state-polling or runtime-chat logic downstream.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:800-808: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 808 as the first substantive operation; a 409 at this call aborts the probe before any evidence can be written.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:102-110: contract requires vmIdPresent === true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready'] — neither assertion can be evaluated because the agent was never created.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — Eval probe org has accumulated 100 swarm agents (live or leaked) and hit the hard quota enforced by the swarm backend. Each eval run creates an agent; if cleanup (withCleanup) failed on prior runs, orphaned agents accumulate against the quota.
SECONDARY — A prior eval run's cleanup step failed silently, leaving one or more agents un-deleted and incrementally consuming quota until the limit was reached.
TERTIARY — The quota limit of 100 was recently lowered by a backend configuration change, causing an org that was previously under the limit to now be over it.

LOW CONFIDENCE — Commit 6b9c8b0 ('feat(observability): separate feature health from runtime evidence') touched all three implicated eval files (features.json, check-expectations.json, run-status-probes.mjs) roughly 7 hours before the failure; however, the suspect-change record shows no candidateTouchedPaths matching the eval runner logic and no matchedNeedles, so a causal link to the quota error is not supported by the supplied evidence.

The remote-agent-state probe depends on successfully creating a remote agent before it can poll state; because creation failed at the API boundary, the probe exited before writing any evidence, causing a complete contract gap for all four required fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state). This is an eval-infrastructure failure against the production-api environment: no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so a broader production outage cannot be asserted from this data alone.

investigations.title: Image Generation Stream Eval Failure: SESSION_OPEN_FAILED (404) on /api/generate/image/stream in production-api Runtime
investigations.summary: The AURA observability eval for check `image-generation-stream` (feature `media-generation`, runtime `production-api`) failed because the agent runtime returned a 404 on the `/api/generate/image/stream` endpoint, emitting a `SESSION_OPEN_FAILED` error frame instead of the expected `generation_completed` frame and image URL artifact. This is an eval-infrastructure failure localized to the `production-api` harness endpoint reachability; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigations.rootCause: The eval probe in `infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs` (lines 904–921) issued an SSE request to `/api/generate/image/stream` against the `production-api` runtime environment. The server responded with HTTP 404, which the stream translated into a `generation_error` frame with code `SESSION_OPEN_FAILED` and the message "agent runtime endpoint not found (404): the harness is unreachable or running an incompatible version." Because the session could not be opened, no `generation_completed` frame was emitted and no image URL was produced, causing both required evidence keys (`frameTypes`, `imageUrlPresent`) to be absent and the contract assertions to fail. The most likely immediate cause is that the agent runtime harness backing `/api/generate/image/stream` in the `production-api` environment is either not deployed, deployed at a different base URL than the eval runner is configured to use (`LOCAL_HARNESS_URL` / `SWARM_BASE_URL`), or is running an incompatible API version that no longer exposes this route. Commit 6b9c8b0 touched workflow and harness setup files (including `.github/actions/setup-harness-sibling/action.yml` and `.github/workflows/aura-observability.yml`) and is a low-confidence hypothesis that a misconfiguration was introduced there, but this is not proven by the available eval or source evidence.
